title: Hedged session cutover and SLO-aware traffic diversion for active-active edge
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Design and implement a hedged, session-preserving cutover mechanism for active-active hosted API gateways that shifts traffic based on SLO budget, preserves in-flight streaming sessions, and integrates with circuit breakers and load-shedding policies. Goal is to enable predictable region-to-region diversion during capacity or perf incidents while avoiding tail-latency explosions and request duplication for stateful sessions.
context: We operate active-active edge gateways in multiple regions. Current diversion behavior is coarse: blunt traffic drains or immediate failover which breaks streaming sessions and spikes tail latency under load. Recently observed incidents where partial region degradation caused client-side reconnect storms, KV cache inconsistencies, and doubled token billing. We need a cutover that 1) preserves session continuity where possible, 2) enforces SLO-aware traffic shifts to avoid exhausting tail-budgets, and 3) integrates with existing circuit breakers and load-shedding layers.
proposal: Introduce a Hedged Cutover Controller (HCC) in the gateway fleet that performs SLO-aware, staged traffic shifts with session steering. Key behaviors: pre-clean snapshot of active KV/session leases, a temporary hedging proxy to forward in-flight streams with token-preserving handoff, progressive weight ramp controlled by per-route tail latency SLO budgets, and a hard-eviction path if stream handoff exceeds a safety timeout. HCC coordinates with the circuit-breaker service: when a region's error-rate or latency breaches configured thresholds, HCC performs a staged diversion (0 -> 5% -> 25% -> 75% -> 100%) with observability gates at each step. Load-shedding policies will be applied preferentially to best-effort routes during early ramp phases and tightened only if regional tail-budget consumption grows. For streaming sessions, we add a short-lived proxy token that allows the destination region to stitch the session with preserved KV cache prefixes. If stitch fails within N seconds, client receives a graceful error plus suggested retry metadata to minimize reconnect storms.
tradeoffs: Pros: smoother operator-controlled shifts, preserved sessions when feasible, lower reconnect churn. Cons: increased implementation complexity, transient additional latency for hedged requests, possible duplicate work during overlap window. We accept temporary additional CPU and KV traffic during the ramp for improved availability and lower customer-visible errors. Operational complexity reduced by encoding safe defaults and automating rollback on gate failures.
acceptance_criteria: HCC can perform a staged diversion across two regions with configurable ramp steps and gate checks
Active streaming sessions can be stitched to target region within safety timeout for >= 80% of test cases in CI chaos tests
No spike > 1.5x in 99p token cost observed in canary compared to baseline for equivalent traffic
Automated rollback triggers on tail-latency or error-rate threshold breach at any ramp step
End-to-end telemetry (latency, error-rate, active-sessions, KV-sync errors) visible in Console dashboards
implementation_steps: Spec HCC API and state machine: pre-flight checks, snapshot, ramp steps, rollback criteria
Add short-lived session-stitch token flow between source and target gateways (secure, audited)
Implement ephemeral hedging proxy component in edge fleet to forward in-flight streams
Extend circuit-breaker to expose ramp gate signals and region health scores
Integrate KV prefix snapshot and merge primitives for session data; add backpressure for KV sync
Implement diversion orchestration endpoints and CLI for ops (start/abort/status)
Add per-route default policies for load-shedding preference during ramps
Add robust observability: per-ramp-step events, stitched-session success/failure, stitch latencies
End-to-end tests and chaos suite (net partition, kv lag, high-tail-latency injection)
Rollout canary to non-critical tenants, iterate, then wider rollout
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (alpha): internal canary on dev overlay; no customer traffic; iterate on shape
Phase 1 (canary customers): enable HCC with read-only hedging on 1% traffic; strict rollback gates
Phase 2 (broader canary): 5% of production customers; enable streaming stitch and KV sync; monitor 72h
Phase 3 (regional opt-in): allow selected regions to opt-in for active-active cutovers; continue monitoring
Phase 4 (global default): enable by default with safe limits and observability; full runbook published
Abort conditions: any ramp step with >5% increase in 99p latency or >0.5% uptick in client reconnects for streaming routes will trigger automatic rollback
monitoring_and_alerting: Per-route 99p latency delta vs baseline (alert if >20ms increase at ramp step)
Stitched session success rate (alert if < 80% over 5m rolling window)
KV-sync error rate and sync duration percentiles (alert on errors or long-tail >2s)
Region health composite score (latency, error-rate, CPU, mem); HCC uses this for gate decisions
Token accounting metric to detect double-billing (alert if duplicated tokens >0.01% in window)
Circuit-breaker state changes and number of shed requests per route (dashboards + paging for P0 incidents)
testing_plan: Unit tests for HCC state transitions and gate evaluation logic
Integration test: hedged proxy + session-stitch flow end-to-end in staging
Chaos test: simulate KV lag and ensure graceful degrade and rollback
Load test: progressive ramp under peak qps to measure tail-latency and cost delta
Canary scenarios: scripted streaming sessions that assert session continuity or graceful, informative errors
Security review and pen-test on session-stitch token exchange
notes: 2025-03-03: Initial design review with Runtime and Console teams — consensus on safety gates. 2025-03-06: Spike for session-stitch prototype shows 78% success with current KV merge; need retry/backoff changes in KV sync. 2025-03-09: Security requested shorter token TTL and additional audit events — implemented. Next: complete hedging proxy integration and add canary CLI flag.
